calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.70(1), 10.10.60.70(1) and the zone lot coverage regulations, on a lot with a residential building (not an apartment building) and a garden suite building, option (A): the area covered by all buildings and structures must not exceed 45 percent.
calculation_handling.gaps: (A) and (B) are alternative compliance paths ('or'); the owner may meet either. The DSL has no choice operator across units, so this 45 percent of ALL buildings must not be combined with (B) as two simultaneous limits. Zones are those of the displaced regulations (R, RD/RS, RT, RM chapters), not named here, so zones are left empty.

units.disclosure: With a garden suite you may use either a 45% total coverage cap for all buildings, or the separate (B) caps; we show both options.

calculation_handling.description: Option (B): the garden suite building is excluded from the overall lot coverage; all ancillary buildings combined, including the garden suite, may not exceed 20 percent of the lot area; and the residential building's maximum lot coverage is the Lot Coverage Overlay Map value if mapped, otherwise no lot coverage applies to it.
calculation_handling.gaps: Two statements with different subjects on one target: the first (overlay or unregulated) applies to the residential building only, the second (20 pct) to all ancillary buildings combined. They must not be min-combined. Alternative path to (A).

units.disclosure: Under option (B), your house follows the Lot Coverage Overlay Map (or no limit if unmapped) and all accessory buildings together, including the garden suite, may cover at most 20% of the lot.

150.7.60.70(1).explanation: If you add a garden suite, lot coverage can be met in one of two ways: all buildings together cover no more than 45% of the lot, or the garden suite is left out of the house's coverage, the house follows the coverage map value (none if unmapped), and all accessory buildings together, including the garden suite, cover no more than 20%.
